He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. ==College career== In his senior season at [[Spring Valley High School (South Carolina)|Spring Valley High School]], he was named to the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] roster and scored 14 points. He committed to [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/04/01/cheick-diallo-leads-east-to-mcdonalds-all-american-game-victory/|title=Cheick Diallo leads East to McDonald's All-American Game victory|access-date=April 2, 2015|date=April 1, 2015|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} ESPN ranked him the 21st best recruit in his class. His father, Perry Dozier, was a basketball player for South Carolina in the 1980s.{{cite news|last1=Caraviello|first1=David|title=At South Carolina, P.J. Dozier's transition to college basketball well underway|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/at-south-carolina-p-j-dozier-s-transition-to-college/article_0d551d8b-3960-555b-b151-83a6caa2e812.html|access-date=April 4, 2017|work=The Post and Courier|date=June 28, 2015}} In his sophomore season, along with guard [[Sindarius Thornwell]], Dozier was an important part of South Carolina's improbable Final Four appearance. He scored 21 points against [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] in the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news|last1=Cloninger|first1=David|title=Dozier playing his best at the right time|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article141825689.html|access-date=April 4, 2017|work=Charlotte Observer|date=March 30, 2017}} Dozier was named to the East Region All-Tournament Team. In the 77–73 loss to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] in the Final Four, Dozier had 17 points.{{cite news|title=Dozier doesn't know if he'll go pro|url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article142225384.html|access-date=April 4, 2017|work=The State|date=April 1, 2017}} At the conclusion of his sophomore season, Dozier announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|first=Gary |last=Parrish|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nba-draft-2017-south-carolinas-pj-dozier-to-sign-with-agent-remain-in-draft/|title=NBA Draft 2017: South Carolina's PJ Dozier to sign with agent, remain in draft|website=cbssports.com|access-date= November 13, 2018|date=April 17, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2017–2018)=== [[File:PJ Dozier - 2018 NBA Summer League.png|thumb|left|150px|Dozier at the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].]] After going undrafted in [[2017 NBA draft]], Dozier signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. He signed a contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on August 8, 2017.{{cite news|last1=Karalla|first1=Bobby|title=Mavericks sign guard P.J. Dozier |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-guard-p-j-dozier/|access-date=August 8, 2017|work=[[Dallas Mavericks]]|date=August 8, 2017}} He was released on October 14, 2017, before agreeing to a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] two days later. Under the terms of the deal, Dozier split time between the Thunder and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]]. Dozier would make his NBA debut on February 8, 2018, in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. ===Boston Celtics (2018–2019)=== On August 21, 2018, Dozier signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |title=Celtics Sign PJ Dozier to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-pj-dozier-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 21, 2018 |date=August 21, 2018}} In February 2019, Dozier was named to the All-NBA G League team, the equivalent of All-Star.[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article226091980.html PJ Dozier is one of G-League’s best this season] February 11, 2019 On June 30, 2019, the Celtics declined to extend his contract, thus making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web |title=Boston declining qualifying offer to P.J. Dozier |url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-boston-declining-qualifying-offer-to-p-j-dozier/ |website=clutchpoints.com |access-date= June 30, 2019 |date= June 30, 2019}} On July 4, Dozier was included in the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]' Summer League team.{{cite web|title=Former Gamecock PJ Dozier gets shot with another NBA team|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article232284302.html|access-date = July 4, 2019|date = July 4, 2019}} ===Denver Nuggets (2019–2022)=== On August 13, 2019, Dozier signed a one-year contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets sign Tyler Cook and P.J. Dozier|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-tyler-cook-pj-dozier-081319|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 13, 2019|date=August 13, 2019}} He was assigned to the [[Windy City Bulls]] for the start of the [[NBA G League]] season.{{cite web |last1=Kessenich |first1=Joe |title=WINDY CITY BULLS ANNOUNCE 2019-20 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER FOR TEAM'S FOURTH SEASON |url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-announce-2019-20-opening-night-roster-for-teams-fourth-season/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 5, 2019 |date=November 7, 2019}} On January 11, 2020, Dozier had a game-high 32 points, nine assists, eight rebounds, two steals and one block in a 120–112 win over the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite news |title=Nuggets' PJ Dozier: Goes off in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-pj-dozier-goes-off-in-g-league/ |access-date=January 12, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 11, 2020}} In his Denver debut on January 15, Dozier finished with 12 points as he filled in for the injured [[Jamal Murray]].{{cite news |last1=Graham |first1=Pat |title=PJ Dozier delivers in Denver debut, helps Nuggets beat Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article239342028.html |access-date=January 16, 2020 |work=The State |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 16, 2020}} On June 30, the Denver Nuggets converted his two-way contract to a multi-year NBA contract.[https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/dozier-converted-contract-20200625 Nuggets sign P.J. Dozier to NBA contract] NBA.com, June 2020 On November 23, 2021, during a 100–119 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Dozier tore his left ACL. The next day, it was confirmed that the tear was a season-ending injury.{{Cite web|title=Nuggets say guard PJ Dozier out for season with torn ACL|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/nuggets-guard-pj-dozier-season-001219834.html|url-status=dead|access-date=November 24, 2021|website=Yahoo Sports|archive-date=November 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125013340/https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/nuggets-guard-pj-dozier-season-001219834.html}} On January 19, 2022, Dozier was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade involving the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-bol-bol-pj-dozier-three-team-deal|title=Celtics Acquire Bol Bol, P.J. Dozier in Three-Team Deal|work=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2022}} On February 10, 2022, Dozier was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]], without appearing in a game for the Celtics.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-boston-celtics-trade-bol-bol-pj-dozier-second-round-pick-cash-considerations-waive-michael-carter-williams-etwaun-moore-20220209|title=Orlando Magic Acquire Bol Bol, P.J. Dozier, Future Second Round Draft Pick and Cash Considerations From Boston|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022}} He was waived by the Magic following the trade.{{Cite tweet |user=Magic_PR |number=1491868590416568321 |title=The @OrlandoMagic have waived guard P.J. Dozier. #MagicTogether|date=February 10, 2022}} ===Iowa Wolves (2022–2023)=== On September 17, 2022, Dozier signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |title=Sources - Free Agent P.J. (2023–2024)=== On August 12, 2023, Dozier signed a one-year deal with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), the [[ABA League|Adriatic League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Pi Džej Doužer je novo pojačanje Partizana Mozzart Bet|url=https://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/3511/pi-dzej-douzer-je-novo-pojacanje-partizana-mozzart-bet|website=KKPartizan.rs|date=August 12, 2023|access-date=August 12, 2023|language=Serbian}} In his first season with the club, he averaged 9.2 points, 3 rebounds and 3.1 assists over 33 EuroLeague games. ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2024)=== On July 15, 2024, Dozier signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign PJ Dozier|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-pj-dozier|website=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2024|access-date=July 16, 2024}} However, he was waived on December 28, after nine appearances.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive PJ Dozier|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-pj-dozier|website=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2024|access-date=December 28, 2024}} ===Anadolu Efes (2025–present)=== On January 12, 2025, Dozier signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{cite web|title=PJ Dozier Anadolu Efes’te...|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/pj-dozier-anadolu-efes-te|website=AnadoluEfesSK.org|date=January 12, 2025|access-date=January 12, 2025|language=tr}} On June 12, Dozier's contract was extended through 2027 by the club.{{cite web |title=PJ Dozier to stay with Efes until 2027 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1837025/pj-dozier-to-stay-with-efes-until-2027/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=12 June 2025 |language=en |date=11 June 2025}} On November 10, 2025, Dozier suffered a right [[hamstring]] tear. {{cite web |title=P.J. Dozier out long-term with an injury |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234724-pj-dozier-out-long-term-with-an-injury.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}} ==Career
